source.title: Generalization Beyond Feature Alignment: Concept Activation-Guided Contrastive Learning
source.authors: Y. Liu; Chris Xing Tian; Haoliang Li; Shi-Qi Wang

record.tranche_reason: The study uses neuron clustering and activation concepts as tools in its contrastive-learning method, but does not test the claim’s audit shares or the reliability of neuron explanations on held-out activations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports neuron-coverage outcomes and a qualitative example of a neuron becoming a concept detector; these bear on neuron activation but do not measure the proportion of neurons with one or more understandable jobs. Its feature-diversity and classification-accuracy results do not directly measure the claim versions. No labels are given because the study does not test a version.
record.test_reason: The study uses neuron-as-concept-detector ideas (Network Dissection, neuron clustering) as a tool for a domain-generalization contrastive loss and reports its own method's accuracy, feature diversity and neuron coverage. It never measures what share of neurons have one, two or no understandable jobs. It does not analyse canonical polysemantic neurons, build circuits, or score explanations on held-out activations.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that CoCo relaxes element-wise feature alignment, improves feature diversity and generalization across contrastive DG methods and benchmarks, and broadens neuron coverage, which they link to better generalization.
record.recipe_differences: This is not an audit of neuron poles or a held-out explanation test. It clusters visual-model neurons from activation patterns and uses those clusters to train a concept-level contrastive objective for domain generalization.
record.method_sensitivity: Neuron coverage is compared across datasets and against random concept clusters; the reported results say coverage is higher with the proposed clustering on all plotted datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: In ResNet-50 domain-generalization fine-tuning, CoCo raises the share of neurons that activate on the training set (e.g. +11.5% for SelfReg on PACS). Random clusters give lower coverage. One newly activated neuron (unit 312) appears to become a bird detector by step 3000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Concept-level contrastive fine-tuning increases neuron coverage in vision models, and newly activated neurons can come to detect visual concepts.

record.problems: Neuron coverage is a proxy, not a direct measure of how many neurons have a clear, stable, human-nameable job. The coverage curves are shown without stated numeric values except for the PACS summary; no held-out explanation-accuracy test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Left out classification-accuracy tables, feature-diversity results, and computation-time comparisons because they do not measure neuron interpretability shares or held-out neuron explanations. No additional Figure 6 examples are separately described in the text.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or of job shares.
No language models; no interpretability shares across models or scales.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron; no pose or recursive-generalization analysis.
No interpretable-neuron share by tool or architecture. The CLIP backbone comparison concerns accuracy only.
No attribution graphs; no comparison with replacement models.
No test of whether explanations predict where neurons fire.

record.verdict_notes: Domain-generalization methods paper in vision. It cites the neuron-interpretability literature (Network Dissection) as motivation and assumes many neurons act as concept detectors. It supplies no evidence bearing on any claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B neuron poles or estimate the proportions with one job, two related jobs, or unknown jobs.
Does not compare interpretability shares across language models, dense or mixture-of-experts architectures, or model scales.
Does not analyze InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.

Does not estimate the share of interpretable neurons or test the essay’s proposed causes or InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates. Its architecture comparison concerns downstream accuracy, not interpretability share.
Does not test attribution graphs built from a model’s own neurons or compare them with a trained replacement model.
Does not test explanations against held-out activating examples or measure whether they predict where neurons fire.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.
